newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore July oil output down 12.8 pct over June.
newsitem.headline: Singapore July oil output down 12.8 pct over June.

text.p: Singapore's petroleum product output in July was down 12.8 percent over June, the Economic Development Board (EDB) said on Tuesday.
It said in a statement that output fell as two major refineries underwent maintenance shutdowns in July.
"Despite the July decline, the industry's cumulative output for the first seven months of 1996 expanded by 8.2 percent," the EDB said.
Industry sources said the decline in output for July was in line with expectations as Shell had brought down a 200,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) crude distillation unit (CDU) for maintenance.
The CDU was shut down on July 8 for a month-long scheduled maintenance.
In addition to the Shell shutdown, other refiners in Singapore cut back refining runs due to poor margins.
Mobil Singapore reduced runs at its 280,000-bpd CDU by 10,000 bpd in mid-June and Esso cut runs by 15 percent at its 230,000-bpd refinery in early July.
Both Mobil and Shell have brought operating rates back to full capacity as margins returned to the black. Esso is still maintaining its 15-percent cut.
